commits.message:
feat(collector): the host's collector holds each session's world state and hands it to the renderer (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.kcp) (#712)

* refactor(facts): the facts document is WorldState, the seam between the host and a renderer (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.kcp)

* feat(collector): the host's collector holds each session's world state and hands it to the renderer (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.kcp)

A session's lanes and the stamp of its world state move to the host. One
collector record per session declares the built-in lanes at the keys its
newest request names and each plugin source the renderer's last output
subscribed to, stamps one world state from what they hold, and hands every
stamp that moved to the renderer as a `world-state` event. A request is
delivered on arrival with the world state read at its own keys. The
renderer keeps a world-state store its views read, answers `retire` by
closing the session's view, and says on every output which plugin sources
its open views need read. The session's lifetime is the collector's sweep:
a session no request named across a whole sweep, with no open feed, is
retired.

The view no longer declares, holds or stamps, and the render cache's idle
sweep is gone; a request's wait reads the world-state store.

* fix(collector): a source the host has not read yet draws pending, and a request is stamped once (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.kcp)

The host learns a view's plugin sources from the output of the turn that
opened it, so that turn's world state carries none of them. The payload
projected only the sources the world state carried, so the opening turn
drew such a source as missing (a failed read) rather than pending. The
payload now projects every source the view's config declares, and one the
world state does not carry yet is not read yet. The render event counts
the same set.

A request's stamp and the stamp of each landing now take one read of the
owners, so the reaction a request's declaration wakes finds the read the
request already stamped instead of reading and stamping again. The
record's locator lives only in its declaration.

The demo subscribes its view's sources as a turn's output does, so its
frames read the config's plugin sources. The law marker over the view's
binding is restored.

* fix(collector): a retire whose turn threw keeps the session, and a reload subscribes its successors (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.kcp)

A retire whose renderer turn threw may leave the renderer holding the
session's document. Dropping the record anyway made the next request open
a new record at seq 1, which the renderer's store refuses on every request
after. The record now goes only once the retire was answered, and a
request revives it from the document it kept.

A reload opens its successors outside any turn, so no output carried
their subscriptions, and a source the reload added went unread until an
unrelated turn answered. The daemon's reload observer now hands the
cache's subscriptions to the collector, whole, as an output does, marked
as an exception until config reaches the renderer as an event.

The demo closes its collector on every exit, and the collector reads a
locator's fields by spreading it instead of copying them one by one.

* fix(daemon): drop the reload's subscription take, which ran inside request turns (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.kcp)

The reload observer also fires for an entry a request opens, inside that
request's turn, so taking the cache's subscriptions there could deliver a
nested world-state turn into the request's own. A view that opens outside
any turn is subscribed by the next turn's output, as the plan states; the
data-sources memory now says so for reloads and follows. Two comments that
named the removed single-turn stamp are corrected.
